title: 'I Voted' and 'Future Voter' sticker contest winners announced in Sedgwick County - NewsBreak
text:
By Ryan Newton ,
10 hours ago
WICHITA, Kan. (KSNW) — Sedgwick County Election Commissioner Laura Rainwater announced the winners of the voting sticker contest at Wednesday’s Board of County Commissioners meeting.
This year, the contest was open to all student age groups and included “Future Voter” stickers. The stickers will be given to children who accompany an adult to the polls.
“I Voted” sticker contest (Sixth to 12th grade) Rylin Dehncke, a sophomore at Maize South High School, won the contest for the “I Voted” sticker, which was open to students in sixth through 12th grades.
Dehncke’s colorful design showcases multiple Kansas elements, including the state bird of Kansas, the western meadowlark; a barn; grain bin; airplane; wheat stalk; sunflower; the state motto, “Ad Astra Per Aspera”; and a road leading through a prairie to the Kansas State Capitol building.
Riley McAlister, a ninth grader at Derby High School, and Willa Lorenson, a junior at Valley Center High School, tied for second place. Aubryella Escoto, an eighth grader at Derby North Middle School, finished third.

(Courtesy: Sedgwick County) “Future Voter” sticker contest (Kindergarten through fifth grade) Penelope Gaeddert, a third-grade student at Colwich Elementary School, is the winner of the first “Future Voter” sticker contest.
Gaeddert’s design features an American buffalo, the Kansas state animal, in a field of sunflowers and a blue sky under the words “Future Voter.”
Sophia Solorzano, a fifth-grade student at Isley Traditional Magnet, won second place. Third place went to Isley fifth grader Adalynn Renich and St. Elizabeth Ann Seton fourth grader Clara Lies.

The artwork submitted had to be original and nonpartisan and incorporate the words “I Voted” or “Future Voter.”
